name: Nenets

ancestors.notes: Descent per Glottolog classification of Tundra Nenets (nene1249).

notes: Research. Tundra Nenets is a Samoyedic language of the Uralic family, written in an extended Russian Cyrillic alphabet (Salminen 1993, 1997). Beyond the base letters the map covers Ӈ (velar nasal) and the two apostrophe letters that write the glottal-stop phonemes — the single ʼ (voiceless/nasalizable glottal stop) and the double ˮ — both rendered as ʔ; the voiced/nasalized versus voiceless glottal distinction is not separated. ⟨а⟩ is phonetically back [ɑ], ⟨э⟩ is [æ], and the reduced vowel ⟨ӑ⟩ is [ə] (Salminen 1997) — the pre-upgrade map used [a]/[e] and omitted ⟨ӑ⟩ entirely, its single largest source of error. As in Russian, the iotated letters е/ё/ю/я spell a glide+vowel word-initially or after a vowel, but after a consonant they instead spell that consonant's palatalization plus the plain vowel (тибя [tʲibʲɑ], нямю [ɲɑmʲu]); this is modelled with an `after_consonant` positional override on the vowels plus `followed_by: palatal` allophone rules palatalising the preceding consonant. Word stress falls on the last syllable of the (disyllabic-dominant) stem in the sampled forms (Salminen 1997); marked here as final by default. NorthEuraLex's Value field also wraps a lexically-conditioned but currently-unpronounced final consonant in parentheses for some citation forms (e.g. ⟨няʼ(н)⟩) — this is a dictionary citation convention, not part of Nenets orthography, and the bracketed letters are left unmapped rather than modelled as if they were spelling.
